## Technology Stack Analysis

### Plugin System Architecture

Claude Code plugins are **self-contained directory bundles** that extend the Claude Code CLI through six orthogonal extension points. The architecture follows a composition-over-inheritance model where each plugin is a directory containing a manifest (`plugin.json`) plus optional component directories. Plugins are loaded at startup, cached at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`, and namespaced to prevent conflicts.

**Core Architectural Insight**: The plugin system is *not* a traditional code-level plugin API with interfaces to implement. It's a **declarative configuration system** — markdown files, JSON manifests, and shell scripts. No TypeScript compilation. No build step. Just files in the right directory structure.

_Confidence: HIGH — verified against official docs and 13 official plugins in the repository_
_Source: [Claude Code Plugin Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Six Extension Points (The Plugin Primitives)

| Extension | Weight | Loading | Format | Cohezion Analog |
|-----------|--------|---------|--------|-----------------|
| **Skills** | Lightest | Model-invoked (automatic) | `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | PRIME skills |
| **Commands** | Light | User-invoked (`/name`) | `commands/<name>.md` | `/spec`, `/commit` |
| **Agents** | Medium | Model/user-invoked | `agents/<name>.md` with frontmatter | Subagent types |
| **Hooks** | Medium | Event-driven (automatic) | `hooks/hooks.json` → shell/python | `.claude/hooks/` |
| **MCP Servers** | Heavy | Auto-started on plugin enable | `.mcp.json` | `.mcp.json` |
| **LSP Servers** | Heavy | Auto-started on plugin enable | `.lsp.json` | N/A (new) |

**Key Design Properties:**
- **Skills** are the token-cheapest extension — they only load into context when Claude determines relevance. Frontmatter controls: `disable-model-invocation: true` makes them user-only.
- **Agents** have full subagent semantics: their own system prompt, model selection (`model: sonnet|opus|haiku`), tool restrictions (`tools: Glob, Grep, Read`), and color identifiers.
- **Hooks** support 13 event types including `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `Stop`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `TaskCompleted`, and `TeammateIdle`.
- **Hook types**: `command` (shell), `prompt` (LLM evaluation), and `agent` (agentic verifier with tool access).

_Source: [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference), [Official GitHub](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins)_

### Plugin Manifest Schema (`plugin.json`)

```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name",           // REQUIRED: kebab-case identifier + namespace
  "version": "1.0.0",              // semver
  "description": "Brief purpose",
  "author": { "name": "...", "email": "...", "url": "..." },
  "homepage": "...",
  "repository": "...",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["tag1", "tag2"],
  "commands": ["./custom/cmd.md"],  // Additional paths (supplement defaults)
  "agents": "./custom/agents/",
  "skills": "./custom/skills/",
  "hooks": "./config/hooks.json",   // Or inline object
  "mcpServers": "./mcp-config.json", // Or inline object
  "lspServers": "./.lsp.json",
  "outputStyles": "./styles/"
}
```

**Critical detail**: Custom paths *supplement* default directories, they don't replace them. If `commands/` exists at root AND `"commands": ["./extra/"]` is specified, both are loaded.

**Environment variable**: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolves to the plugin's absolute installation path. Essential for hook scripts and MCP server configs.

_Source: [Plugins Reference — Manifest Schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Agent Definition Format

Agent markdown files use YAML frontmatter for configuration:

```yaml
---
name: code-architect
description: Designs feature architectures by analyzing codebase patterns
tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, WebSearch
model: sonnet
color: green
---

System prompt content follows...
```

**Key fields**: `name`, `description`, `tools` (whitelist), `model` (override), `color` (UI identifier).

**Pattern from official `feature-dev` plugin**: 3 specialized agents (`code-explorer`, `code-architect`, `code-reviewer`) with distinct tool restrictions and model assignments. The architect agent uses Sonnet with read-only tools, demonstrating least-privilege design.

_Source: [feature-dev agents](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/feature-dev/agents)_

### Hook System Architecture

Hooks are the most powerful extension point for autonomous behavior. The `hooks.json` format:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/script.py"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Exit code semantics for `PreToolUse`**: Exit 0 = allow tool, Exit 2 = block tool and show stderr as message. This enables **guardrail plugins** that can prevent operations.

**13 Available Events:**

| Event | Trigger | Cohezion Relevance |
|-------|---------|-------------------|
| `SessionStart` | Session begins | Context injection, sovereignty checks |
| `PreToolUse` | Before any tool | Security guardrails, alignment checks |
| `PostToolUse` | After successful tool | Auto-formatting, metrics recording |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | After tool failure | Error tracking, circuit breakers |
| `Stop` | Agent attempts to stop | Autonomous loop control |
| `SubagentStart` | Subagent spawns | Journey tracking, resource governance |
| `SubagentStop` | Subagent completion | Metrics collection |
| `PreCompact` | Before context compression | State preservation |
| `TaskCompleted` | Task marked complete | Verification triggers |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User sends prompt | Input validation |
| `TeammateIdle` | Team agent goes idle | Load balancing |
| `Notification` | System notification | Alert routing |
| `PermissionRequest` | Permission dialog shown | Auto-approval policies |

_Source: [security-guidance plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/security-guidance), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Settings System (`settings.json`)

Plugins can ship default settings that activate when the plugin is enabled:

```json
{ "agent": "security-reviewer" }
```

This **overrides the main thread agent** — the plugin's agent becomes the primary conversational interface with its own system prompt, tools, and model. Settings from `settings.json` take priority over those in `plugin.json`.

**Implication for Cohezion**: A plugin could activate a "Cohezion Sovereign Agent" as the default, embedding the Charter and Constitution into every session automatically.

_Confidence: HIGH — verified in official docs_
_Source: [Plugins Docs — Settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins)_

### Distribution and Marketplace Architecture

Plugins distribute through **marketplaces** — Git repositories containing a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` that indexes available plugins:

**Installation scopes:**

| Scope | Location | Sharing |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `user` | `~/.claude/settings.json` | Personal, all projects |
| `project` | `.claude/settings.json` | Team-shared via VCS |
| `local` | `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project-only, gitignored |
| `managed` | Managed settings | Read-only |

**CLI commands**: `claude plugin install`, `uninstall`, `enable`, `disable`, `update` — all supporting `--scope` flag.

**Caching**: Marketplace plugins are copied to `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`. Path traversal outside plugin root is blocked. Symlinks are honored during copy (enables shared dependencies).

_Source: [Plugin Marketplaces](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Agent SDK Integration

The Claude Agent SDK (Python + TypeScript) can **programmatically load plugins** into agent sessions:

- Plugins loaded via `--plugin-dir` or marketplace
- Commands auto-namespaced: `plugin-name:command-name`
- MCP servers auto-started
- Skills auto-discovered by model
- Custom tools via in-process MCP servers (Python functions or TypeScript `tool()` helpers)

**Implication**: Cohezion's `CompoundExecutor` could leverage the Agent SDK to load plugins programmatically, adding compound engineering capabilities to any Claude agent session.

_Source: [Agent SDK Plugins Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/plugins), [Agent SDK Overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview)_

- **9,000+ plugins** across official marketplace, community sites, and GitHub (as of Feb 2026)
- **13 official Anthropic plugins** in the `anthropics/claude-code` repository
- **400+ curated extensions** on buildwithclaude.com
- Public beta since October 2025; plugin format still evolving

_Source: [Composio](https://composio.dev/blog/top-claude-code-plugins), [AI Tool Analysis](https://aitoolanalysis.com/claude-code-plugins/), [Build with Claude](https://www.buildwithclaude.com/plugins)_

| **Elegant Simplicity** | Markdown + JSON, no build step, no compilation | Direct mapping to PRIME skills |

## Integration Patterns Analysis

### Hook Event-Driven Architecture (The Integration Backbone)

The hook system is the deepest integration surface. It operates as a **deterministic event bus** — while Claude's prompt-based instructions are "requests," hooks provide **guaranteed execution** every time an event fires. This distinction is critical for Cohezion's autonomous sovereignty.

**Hook Communication Protocol:**

```
Claude Code Event → Matcher Filter → JSON on stdin → Handler Script → Exit Code + JSON on stdout
```

**Stdin JSON Schema (Common Fields):**

```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/home/user/.claude/projects/.../transcript.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/home/user/my-project",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": { "command": "npm test" }
}
```

**PreToolUse Decision Control (stdout JSON):**

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "allow|deny|escalate",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Human-readable reason",
    "modifiedToolInput": { ... }  // v2.0.10+: modify tool input before execution
  }
}
```

**Exit Code Semantics:**

| Exit Code | Meaning | Effect |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `0` | Success/Allow | Proceed, parse stdout JSON |
| `2` | Block | Deny action, show stderr as error to Claude |
| Other | Non-blocking error | Log to verbose, continue |

_Confidence: HIGH — verified against official hooks reference_
_Source: [Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Hooks Guide](https://claude.com/blog/how-to-configure-hooks)_

### Four Hook Handler Types

| Type | Mechanism | Latency | Use Case |
|------|-----------|---------|----------|
| `command` | Shell script, JSON on stdin | ~50ms | Fast checks, file validation, metrics |
| `http` | POST to URL, JSON body | ~200ms | Remote services, webhooks, APIs |
| `prompt` | Single-turn LLM evaluation | ~2s | Semantic checks, content review |
| `agent` | Subagent with tool access (Read, Grep, Glob) | ~10s+ | Deep verification, multi-file analysis |

**Cohezion Integration Insight**: The `agent` hook type is particularly powerful — it spawns a full subagent with tools like Read, Grep, and Glob to verify conditions. This maps directly to Cohezion's `RequestAlignmentAnalyzer` pattern: an agent hook at `PreToolUse` could check alignment before every action.

**HTTP Hooks** enable external service integration with env var interpolation in headers:

```json
{
  "type": "http",
  "url": "http://localhost:8080/hooks/pre-tool-use",
  "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer $MY_TOKEN" },
  "allowedEnvVars": ["MY_TOKEN"]
}
```

_Source: [Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)_

### 17 Hook Events — Complete Lifecycle Coverage

| Event | Blocks? | Matcher Target | Cohezion Compound Loop Stage |
|-------|---------|----------------|------------------------------|
| `SessionStart` | No | `startup\|resume\|clear\|compact` | Journey initialization |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | **Yes** | N/A | Request alignment check |
| `PreToolUse` | **Yes** | Tool name regex | Constitution enforcement |
| `PermissionRequest` | **Yes** | Tool name | Auto-approval policies |
| `PostToolUse` | No | Tool name regex | Metrics recording, skill refinement trigger |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | No | Tool name regex | Circuit breaker, error tracking |
| `SubagentStart` | No | Agent type | Resource governance, journey tracking |
| `SubagentStop` | No | Agent type | Coherence measurement |
| `Stop` | No | N/A | Autonomous loop control |
| `TeammateIdle` | No | N/A | Load balancing, work distribution |
| `TaskCompleted` | No | N/A | Verification trigger |
| `PreCompact` | No | `manual\|auto` | State preservation before context loss |
| `ConfigChange` | No | Config source | Dynamic reconfiguration |
| `WorktreeCreate` | No | N/A | VCS isolation setup |
| `WorktreeRemove` | No | N/A | Worktree cleanup |
| `SessionEnd` | No | Exit reason | Journey completion, metrics flush |
| `Notification` | No | Notification type | Alert routing |

**Key Discovery**: `PreToolUse` can **modify tool inputs** before execution (v2.0.10+). This is transformative — a Cohezion hook could intercept file writes and inject metadata, modify bash commands to add logging, or transform API calls to add observability.

**Hooks in Skills/Agents Frontmatter**: Hooks can be defined directly in skill or agent YAML frontmatter, scoped to the component's lifecycle:

```yaml
---
name: secure-operations
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "Bash"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "./scripts/security-check.sh"
---
```

_Source: [Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [SmartScope Guide](https://smartscope.blog/en/generative-ai/claude/claude-code-hooks-guide/)_

### MCP Integration Patterns

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard for connecting Claude to external tools and data. Plugins can bundle MCP servers that auto-start when the plugin is enabled.

**Plugin MCP Configuration (`.mcp.json`):**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cohezion-vault": {
      "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/servers/vault-server",
      "args": ["--config", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/config.json"],
      "env": { "VAULT_PATH": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/data" }
    }
  }
}
```

**Tool Search (On-Demand Loading)**: When MCP tool descriptions exceed 10% of context window, Claude Code enables **dynamic tool loading** — tools load on demand rather than preloading all definitions. This is critical for token efficiency when a plugin bundles many MCP tools.

**MCP Tool Naming**: Tools follow `mcp__<server>__<tool>` pattern, matchable in hooks via regex (`mcp__cohezion.*`).

**Resources and Prompts**: MCP servers can expose resources (file-like data accessible via `@` mentions) and prompts (commands accessible via `/mcp__servername__promptname`).

_Source: [Claude Code MCP Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp), [MCP Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers)_

### Subagent and Parallel Execution Patterns

**Agent Tool Semantics**: The main Claude agent spawns subagents via the `Agent` tool. Subagents maintain separate context (isolation), can run in parallel, and can optionally use worktree isolation for filesystem-level independence.

**Agent Frontmatter Configuration:**

```yaml
---
name: code-architect
description: Designs feature architectures
tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch  # Tool whitelist
model: sonnet                                       # Model override
color: green                                        # UI identifier
isolation: worktree                                 # Optional: filesystem isolation
---
```

**Parallel Execution Patterns:**

| Pattern | Mechanism | Example |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| Parallel agents | Multiple `Agent` tool calls in one message | 5 code review agents running simultaneously |
| Background agents | `run_in_background: true` | Long analysis while main thread continues |
| Worktree isolation | `isolation: worktree` in frontmatter | Each agent gets its own git worktree |
| Agent Teams | Structured coordination with Team Lead + Teammates | `TeammateIdle` hook for work distribution |

**Worktree Architecture**: `--worktree` creates isolated branches at `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`. All worktrees share the same `.git` history and remotes. Auto-cleaned on agent completion if no changes. Custom VCS support via `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks.

_Source: [Common Workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows), [Subagents in SDK](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents)_

### Agent SDK Programmatic Integration (Python)

The Agent SDK enables **programmatic plugin loading** — Cohezion's `CompoundExecutor` could load plugins into agent sessions dynamically:

```python
from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, HookMatcher

options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
    system_prompt="Cohezion Sovereign Agent",
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
    plugins=[{"type": "local", "path": "./cohezion-plugin"}],
    hooks=[
        HookMatcher(
            event="PreToolUse",
            matcher="Bash",
            callback=check_bash_command  # Python async function
        )
    ],
    tools=["Read", "Write", "Bash", "Grep"],
    max_turns=50,
    max_budget_usd=0.50
)
```

**Python Custom Tools**: Define tools as Python functions that Claude can invoke:

```python
@tool
async def query_vault(query: str) -> str:
    """Search Cohezion vault for relevant context."""
    return await vault_client.search(query)
```

**Hook Callback Signature**: `async (HookInput, str | None, HookContext) -> HookJSONOutput`

_Source: [Agent SDK Python](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python), [Agent SDK Plugins](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/plugins)_

### Plugin-to-Plugin Interoperability

Plugins are isolated by default but compose naturally:
- Multiple plugins can register hooks on the same event — all run in parallel
- Identical handlers are auto-deduplicated (by command string or URL)
- Plugin MCP servers appear alongside project MCP servers
- Skills from multiple plugins coexist in the same namespace (plugin-prefixed)
- `settings.json` agent override is mutually exclusive (last-enabled wins)

**Security Model**: Hooks are snapshotted at startup. Mid-session modifications trigger a review warning. Enterprise admins can enforce `allowManagedHooksOnly` to block user/project/plugin hooks. Plugin cache prevents path traversal outside plugin root.

_Source: [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Integration Security Patterns

| Mechanism | Protection |
|-----------|------------|
| Hook snapshotting | Prevents mid-session hook modification without review |
| Plugin caching | Copies to `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`, blocks path traversal |
| `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` | Sandboxes plugin file references |
| `allowManagedHooksOnly` | Enterprise control over hook execution |
| Agent tool whitelists | `tools:` field restricts subagent capabilities |
| `permissionDecision: "deny"` | Deterministic action blocking |
| Marketplace review | Automated + manual review for "Verified" badge |

**Cohezion Constitutional Alignment**: The `PreToolUse` + `permissionDecision` pattern maps directly to Constitution enforcement. A Cohezion plugin could implement every Charter rule as a deterministic hook — not a prompt instruction that might be ignored, but a guaranteed check that blocks violating actions.

_Source: [Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

## Architectural Patterns and Design

### Pattern 1: Declarative Markdown-as-Code

The most striking architectural pattern is that **the entire plugin system is declarative markdown**. No TypeScript to compile, no build step, no package manager. The "code" of a plugin is:

- `plugin.json` — JSON metadata
- `SKILL.md` — Markdown instructions with YAML frontmatter
- `agents/*.md` — Markdown system prompts with frontmatter
- `hooks.json` — JSON event configuration → shell/python scripts
- `.mcp.json` — JSON server definitions

**Design Insight**: This is a profound architectural choice. By making the extension format *the same format the LLM processes*, there is zero impedance mismatch between the extension and the runtime. The plugin *is* the prompt. The agent definition *is* the system prompt.

**Cohezion Alignment**: This maps perfectly to PRIME skills. Each PRIME skill at `src/cohezion/skills/*.md` is already a markdown file with structured sections. Converting them to `SKILL.md` format with frontmatter is a **trivial migration** — add a YAML header and restructure sections.

_Source: [Skills Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Pattern 2: Progressive Disclosure Architecture

Skills use a **two-tier loading model** that optimizes token efficiency:

| Level | What Loads | When | Token Cost |
|-------|-----------|------|------------|
| **Descriptions** | YAML frontmatter `description` field only | Always (2% of context window budget) | ~50-100 tokens/skill |
| **Full Content** | Entire `SKILL.md` + supporting files | Only when invoked (by user or model) | ~500-5000 tokens/skill |

This means a plugin with 20 skills costs only ~1,000-2,000 tokens for descriptions, loading full content only when relevant. The budget scales dynamically at 2% of context window with a fallback of 16,000 characters.

**Supporting Files Pattern**: `SKILL.md` keeps the overview; heavy reference material lives in separate files (`reference.md`, `examples.md`, `scripts/`) loaded on-demand:

```
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md           # 50-200 lines, overview + navigation
├── reference.md       # Loaded only when needed
├── examples/          # Loaded only when needed
└── scripts/
    └── helper.py      # Executed, not loaded into context
```

**Cohezion Implication**: PRIME skills can be restructured for progressive disclosure — keep the skill description tight for auto-discovery, move detailed operational instructions to supporting files. This could reduce Cohezion's baseline context footprint by 80%+.

_Source: [Skills Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), [Anthropic's Guide to Building Skills](https://resources.anthropic.com/hubfs/The-Complete-Guide-to-Building-Skill-for-Claude.pdf)_

### Pattern 3: Invocation Control Matrix

The frontmatter fields create a 2x2 control matrix for skill activation:

| | User Can Invoke | User Cannot Invoke |
|---|---|---|
| **Model Can Invoke** | Default (most skills) | `user-invocable: false` — background knowledge |
| **Model Cannot Invoke** | `disable-model-invocation: true` — explicit workflows | Invisible (not useful) |

**Additional Control Dimensions:**
- `allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob` — tool whitelist when skill is active
- `model: haiku` — model override for cost optimization
- `context: fork` — run in isolated subagent context
- `agent: Explore` — specify subagent type for forked execution
- `hooks:` — lifecycle hooks scoped to skill activation

**Cohezion Compound Engineering Pattern**: Combine these controls:
- **PRIME research skills** → `context: fork`, `agent: Explore`, `model: haiku` → cheap, isolated research
- **Deployment skills** → `disable-model-invocation: true` → user-controlled side effects
- **Domain knowledge** → `user-invocable: false` → background context Claude applies automatically
- **Sovereignty checks** → `hooks: PreToolUse` in frontmatter → Constitution enforcement scoped to skill lifecycle

_Source: [Skills Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)_

### Pattern 4: Hierarchical Agent Orchestration

The plugin architecture enables a three-tier agent hierarchy:

```
Plugin settings.json agent → Main Thread Agent (sovereign system prompt)
    ├── Skill with context: fork → Forked Subagent (isolated task)
    ├── Agent tool → Custom Subagent (specialist with tool whitelist)
    │   └── Nested subagent (deeper delegation)
    └── Agent hook → Verification Agent (PreToolUse/TaskCompleted)
```

**Official Pattern (code-review plugin)**: 5 parallel Sonnet agents with distinct specializations:

1. Two CLAUDE.md compliance agents (parallel, Sonnet)
2. One bug scanner (Opus, diff-only)
3. One security/logic analyzer (Opus, broader context)
4. Validation agents for each finding (parallel, model-appropriate)

**Key Design Constraint**: "3-4 subagents maximum" — beyond this, coordination overhead exceeds parallelism benefit. Each task should target 5-15 minutes of work.

**Cohezion Mapping**:

| Cohezion Pattern | Plugin Architecture Equivalent |
|------------------|-------------------------------|
| `CompoundExecutor` | Main thread agent with sovereign system prompt |
| `RequestAlignmentAnalyzer` | `PreToolUse` agent hook |
| `SkillRefiner` | `PostToolUse` hook → metrics → skill file update |
| `RetrospectionEngine` | `SessionEnd` hook → journey analysis |
| `JourneyTracker` | `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` hooks → state tracking |
| `DegradationDetector` | `PostToolUseFailure` hook → circuit breaker |
| Expert Domain Lattice | Agents with specialized tool whitelists + model overrides |

_Source: [Subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents), [code-review plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/code-review), [Hierarchical Orchestration](https://explore.n1n.ai/blog/hierarchical-orchestration-claude-code-agent-teams-2026-02-27)_

### Pattern 5: Event-Driven Compound Loop

Hooks create a **deterministic feedback loop** that maps directly to the compound engineering cycle:

```
SessionStart hook → Initialize journey, load vault context
    ↓
UserPromptSubmit hook → Request alignment analysis
    ↓
PreToolUse hook → Constitution enforcement, input modification
    ↓
PostToolUse hook → Metrics recording, coherence tracking
    ↓
PostToolUseFailure hook → Circuit breaker, degradation detection
    ↓
SubagentStart/Stop hooks → Resource governance, journey tracking
    ↓
TaskCompleted hook → Verification trigger, quality gate
    ↓
PreCompact hook → State preservation before context loss
    ↓
Stop hook → Autonomous loop control (continue/halt decision)
    ↓
SessionEnd hook → Journey completion, metrics flush, skill refinement trigger
```

**Key Architectural Insight**: The `Stop` hook enables autonomous agent loops. The `ralph-wiggum` official plugin demonstrates this — it creates a `/ralph-loop` command and a `Stop` hook that prevents termination until completion criteria are met. Combined with `TeammateIdle` for work distribution, this enables fully autonomous compound engineering cycles.

**PreCompact as State Bridge**: The `PreCompact` hook fires before context compression — the exact point where Cohezion's context continuation protocol needs to save state. A hook here could automatically write continuation files before any context is lost.

_Source: [Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [ralph-wiggum plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/ralph-wiggum)_

### Pattern 6: Dynamic Context Injection

Skills support shell command preprocessing via `` !`command` `` syntax — commands execute before the skill content is sent to Claude:

```yaml
---
name: compound-status
description: Show current compound engineering status
---

## Current State
- Journey position: !`python3 scripts/get_journey_position.py`
- Coherence score: !`python3 scripts/get_coherence.py`
- Active skills: !`python3 scripts/get_active_skills.py`
- Vault context: !`mcp-cli cohezion-vault/vault_find_relevant_context '{"query": "$ARGUMENTS"}'`
```

This enables **live system state injection** — every time the skill activates, it fetches fresh data from Cohezion's compound systems. No stale context, no manual updates.

**String Substitutions Available:**
- `$ARGUMENTS` — user input
- `$ARGUMENTS[N]` / `$N` — positional arguments
- `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}` — session correlation

_Source: [Skills Docs — Dynamic Context](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)_

### Pattern 7: Security Architecture (Guardrails, Not Walls)

A critical insight from the Trail of Bits analysis: **"Hooks are structured prompt injection at opportune times — guardrails, not walls."** They intercept tool calls, inject context, block known-bad patterns, and steer agent behavior, but they are not a security boundary against determined adversaries.

**Layered Security Model for Cohezion:**

| Layer | Mechanism | Strength |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| **Constitution** | `PreToolUse` hook → deny actions violating Charter | Deterministic, guaranteed |
| **Alignment** | `UserPromptSubmit` agent hook → semantic analysis | Probabilistic, model-dependent |
| **Observability** | `PostToolUse` async hook → metrics/audit trail | Non-blocking, comprehensive |
| **Resource** | `SubagentStart` hook → budget/token governance | Deterministic |
| **Recovery** | `PreCompact` hook → state checkpoint | Deterministic |
| **Admin** | `allowManagedHooksOnly` → enterprise enforcement | Infrastructure-level |

**Hook Snapshotting**: Hooks are captured at session start and frozen. Mid-session modifications trigger review warnings. This prevents runtime hook tampering — a Cohezion plugin's Constitutional hooks cannot be altered once a session begins.

_Source: [Trail of Bits config](https://github.com/trailofbits/claude-code-config), [Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)_

### Proposed Cohezion Plugin Architecture

Synthesizing all patterns into a concrete plugin design:

```
cohezion-plugin/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json                  # name: "cohezion", version from pyproject.toml
├── settings.json                    # agent: "cohezion-sovereign" (main thread override)
├── agents/
│   ├── cohezion-sovereign.md        # Charter + Constitution system prompt
│   ├── compound-researcher.md       # model: haiku, tools: Read,Grep,Glob,WebSearch
│   ├── skill-refiner.md             # model: sonnet, tools: Read,Write,Grep
│   └── alignment-checker.md         # model: haiku, tools: Read,Grep (agent hook)
├── skills/
│   ├── compound-loop/
│   │   ├── SKILL.md                 # Compound engineering entry point
│   │   └── reference.md             # Detailed operational guide
│   ├── journey-status/
│   │   └── SKILL.md                 # Dynamic context: !`python3 get_journey.py`
│   ├── retrospection/
│   │   └── SKILL.md                 # context: fork, agent: compound-researcher
│   └── [74 PRIME skills migrated]/
│       └── SKILL.md                 # One per existing PRIME skill
├── hooks/
│   ├── hooks.json                   # Event → handler mapping
│   ├── constitution_guard.py        # PreToolUse: Charter enforcement
│   ├── metrics_recorder.py          # PostToolUse: async metrics to SurrealDB
│   ├── journey_tracker.py           # SubagentStart/Stop: 12D position tracking
│   ├── context_preserver.py         # PreCompact: continuation state save
│   └── session_lifecycle.py         # SessionStart/End: vault context inject/flush
├── .mcp.json                        # cohezion-vault MCP server auto-start
└── README.md
```

**Estimated Token Budget:**
- 74 skill descriptions: ~3,700 tokens (always loaded)
- Sovereign agent system prompt: ~2,000 tokens (always loaded)
- Active skill full content: ~1,000-3,000 tokens (on-demand)
- **Total baseline: ~5,700 tokens** (vs. current CLAUDE.md ~8,000+ tokens)

_Confidence: HIGH — all patterns verified against official documentation and source code_

## Technology Stack Analysis

### Plugin System Architecture

Claude Code plugins are **self-contained directory bundles** that extend the Claude Code CLI through six orthogonal extension points. The architecture follows a composition-over-inheritance model where each plugin is a directory containing a manifest (`plugin.json`) plus optional component directories. Plugins are loaded at startup, cached at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`, and namespaced to prevent conflicts.

**Core Architectural Insight**: The plugin system is *not* a traditional code-level plugin API with interfaces to implement. It's a **declarative configuration system** — markdown files, JSON manifests, and shell scripts. No TypeScript compilation. No build step. Just files in the right directory structure.

_Confidence: HIGH — verified against official docs and 13 official plugins in the repository_
_Source: [Claude Code Plugin Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Six Extension Points (The Plugin Primitives)

| Extension | Weight | Loading | Format | Cohezion Analog |
|-----------|--------|---------|--------|-----------------|
| **Skills** | Lightest | Model-invoked (automatic) | `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | PRIME skills |
| **Commands** | Light | User-invoked (`/name`) | `commands/<name>.md` | `/spec`, `/commit` |
| **Agents** | Medium | Model/user-invoked | `agents/<name>.md` with frontmatter | Subagent types |
| **Hooks** | Medium | Event-driven (automatic) | `hooks/hooks.json` → shell/python | `.claude/hooks/` |
| **MCP Servers** | Heavy | Auto-started on plugin enable | `.mcp.json` | `.mcp.json` |
| **LSP Servers** | Heavy | Auto-started on plugin enable | `.lsp.json` | N/A (new) |

**Key Design Properties:**
- **Skills** are the token-cheapest extension — they only load into context when Claude determines relevance. Frontmatter controls: `disable-model-invocation: true` makes them user-only.
- **Agents** have full subagent semantics: their own system prompt, model selection (`model: sonnet|opus|haiku`), tool restrictions (`tools: Glob, Grep, Read`), and color identifiers.
- **Hooks** support 13 event types including `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `Stop`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `TaskCompleted`, and `TeammateIdle`.
- **Hook types**: `command` (shell), `prompt` (LLM evaluation), and `agent` (agentic verifier with tool access).

_Source: [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference), [Official GitHub](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins)_

### Plugin Manifest Schema (`plugin.json`)

```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name",           // REQUIRED: kebab-case identifier + namespace
  "version": "1.0.0",              // semver
  "description": "Brief purpose",
  "author": { "name": "...", "email": "...", "url": "..." },
  "homepage": "...",
  "repository": "...",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["tag1", "tag2"],
  "commands": ["./custom/cmd.md"],  // Additional paths (supplement defaults)
  "agents": "./custom/agents/",
  "skills": "./custom/skills/",
  "hooks": "./config/hooks.json",   // Or inline object
  "mcpServers": "./mcp-config.json", // Or inline object
  "lspServers": "./.lsp.json",
  "outputStyles": "./styles/"
}
```

**Critical detail**: Custom paths *supplement* default directories, they don't replace them. If `commands/` exists at root AND `"commands": ["./extra/"]` is specified, both are loaded.

Hooks are the most powerful extension point for autonomous behavior. The `hooks.json` format:

## Integration Patterns Analysis

### Hook Event-Driven Architecture (The Integration Backbone)

The hook system is the deepest integration surface. It operates as a **deterministic event bus** — while Claude's prompt-based instructions are "requests," hooks provide **guaranteed execution** every time an event fires. This distinction is critical for Cohezion's autonomous sovereignty.

**Hook Communication Protocol:**

```
Claude Code Event → Matcher Filter → JSON on stdin → Handler Script → Exit Code + JSON on stdout
```

**Stdin JSON Schema (Common Fields):**

```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/home/user/.claude/projects/.../transcript.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/home/user/my-project",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": { "command": "npm test" }
}
```

**PreToolUse Decision Control (stdout JSON):**

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "allow|deny|escalate",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Human-readable reason",
    "modifiedToolInput": { ... }  // v2.0.10+: modify tool input before execution
  }
}
```

**Exit Code Semantics:**

| Exit Code | Meaning | Effect |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `0` | Success/Allow | Proceed, parse stdout JSON |
| `2` | Block | Deny action, show stderr as error to Claude |
| Other | Non-blocking error | Log to verbose, continue |

_Confidence: HIGH — verified against official hooks reference_
_Source: [Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Hooks Guide](https://claude.com/blog/how-to-configure-hooks)_

### Four Hook Handler Types

| Type | Mechanism | Latency | Use Case |
|------|-----------|---------|----------|
| `command` | Shell script, JSON on stdin | ~50ms | Fast checks, file validation, metrics |
| `http` | POST to URL, JSON body | ~200ms | Remote services, webhooks, APIs |
| `prompt` | Single-turn LLM evaluation | ~2s | Semantic checks, content review |
| `agent` | Subagent with tool access (Read, Grep, Glob) | ~10s+ | Deep verification, multi-file analysis |

**Cohezion Integration Insight**: The `agent` hook type is particularly powerful — it spawns a full subagent with tools like Read, Grep, and Glob to verify conditions. This maps directly to Cohezion's `RequestAlignmentAnalyzer` pattern: an agent hook at `PreToolUse` could check alignment before every action.

**HTTP Hooks** enable external service integration with env var interpolation in headers:

```json
{
  "type": "http",
  "url": "http://localhost:8080/hooks/pre-tool-use",
  "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer $MY_TOKEN" },
  "allowedEnvVars": ["MY_TOKEN"]
}
```

### MCP Integration Patterns

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard for connecting Claude to external tools and data. Plugins can bundle MCP servers that auto-start when the plugin is enabled.

**Plugin MCP Configuration (`.mcp.json`):**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cohezion-vault": {
      "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/servers/vault-server",
      "args": ["--config", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/config.json"],
      "env": { "VAULT_PATH": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/data" }
    }
  }
}
```

**Tool Search (On-Demand Loading)**: When MCP tool descriptions exceed 10% of context window, Claude Code enables **dynamic tool loading** — tools load on demand rather than preloading all definitions. This is critical for token efficiency when a plugin bundles many MCP tools.

**MCP Tool Naming**: Tools follow `mcp__<server>__<tool>` pattern, matchable in hooks via regex (`mcp__cohezion.*`).

**Resources and Prompts**: MCP servers can expose resources (file-like data accessible via `@` mentions) and prompts (commands accessible via `/mcp__servername__promptname`).

_Source: [Claude Code MCP Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp), [MCP Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers)_

### Subagent and Parallel Execution Patterns

**Agent Tool Semantics**: The main Claude agent spawns subagents via the `Agent` tool. Subagents maintain separate context (isolation), can run in parallel, and can optionally use worktree isolation for filesystem-level independence.

**Agent Frontmatter Configuration:**

```yaml
---
name: code-architect
description: Designs feature architectures
tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch  # Tool whitelist
model: sonnet                                       # Model override
color: green                                        # UI identifier
isolation: worktree                                 # Optional: filesystem isolation
---
```

**Parallel Execution Patterns:**

| Pattern | Mechanism | Example |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| Parallel agents | Multiple `Agent` tool calls in one message | 5 code review agents running simultaneously |
| Background agents | `run_in_background: true` | Long analysis while main thread continues |
| Worktree isolation | `isolation: worktree` in frontmatter | Each agent gets its own git worktree |
| Agent Teams | Structured coordination with Team Lead + Teammates | `TeammateIdle` hook for work distribution |

**Worktree Architecture**: `--worktree` creates isolated branches at `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`. All worktrees share the same `.git` history and remotes. Auto-cleaned on agent completion if no changes. Custom VCS support via `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks.

_Source: [Common Workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows), [Subagents in SDK](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents)_

The Agent SDK enables **programmatic plugin loading** — Cohezion's `CompoundExecutor` could load plugins into agent sessions dynamically:

### Plugin-to-Plugin Interoperability

Plugins are isolated by default but compose naturally:
- Multiple plugins can register hooks on the same event — all run in parallel
- Identical handlers are auto-deduplicated (by command string or URL)
- Plugin MCP servers appear alongside project MCP servers
- Skills from multiple plugins coexist in the same namespace (plugin-prefixed)
- `settings.json` agent override is mutually exclusive (last-enabled wins)

**Security Model**: Hooks are snapshotted at startup. Mid-session modifications trigger a review warning. Enterprise admins can enforce `allowManagedHooksOnly` to block user/project/plugin hooks. Plugin cache prevents path traversal outside plugin root.

_Source: [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Integration Security Patterns

| Mechanism | Protection |
|-----------|------------|
| Hook snapshotting | Prevents mid-session hook modification without review |
| Plugin caching | Copies to `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`, blocks path traversal |
| `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` | Sandboxes plugin file references |
| `allowManagedHooksOnly` | Enterprise control over hook execution |
| Agent tool whitelists | `tools:` field restricts subagent capabilities |
| `permissionDecision: "deny"` | Deterministic action blocking |
| Marketplace review | Automated + manual review for "Verified" badge |

**Cohezion Constitutional Alignment**: The `PreToolUse` + `permissionDecision` pattern maps directly to Constitution enforcement. A Cohezion plugin could implement every Charter rule as a deterministic hook — not a prompt instruction that might be ignored, but a guaranteed check that blocks violating actions.

_Source: [Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

lines: +The most striking architectural pattern is that **the entire plugin system is declarative markdown**. No TypeScript to compile, no build step, no package manager. The "code" of a plugin is:

+**Design Insight**: This is a profound architectural choice. By making the extension format *the same format the LLM processes*, there is zero impedance mismatch between the extension and the runtime. The plugin *is* the prompt. The agent definition *is* the system prompt.

+**Cohezion Alignment**: This maps perfectly to PRIME skills. Each PRIME skill at `src/cohezion/skills/*.md` is already a markdown file with structured sections. Converting them to `SKILL.md` format with frontmatter is a **trivial migration** — add a YAML header and restructure sections.
+Skills use a **two-tier loading model** that optimizes token efficiency:
+| Level | What Loads | When | Token Cost |
+| **Descriptions** | YAML frontmatter `description` field only | Always (2% of context window budget) | ~50-100 tokens/skill |
+| **Full Content** | Entire `SKILL.md` + supporting files | Only when invoked (by user or model) | ~500-5000 tokens/skill |

+This means a plugin with 20 skills costs only ~1,000-2,000 tokens for descriptions, loading full content only when relevant. The budget scales dynamically at 2% of context window with a fallback of 16,000 characters.
+**Supporting Files Pattern**: `SKILL.md` keeps the overview; heavy reference material lives in separate files (`reference.md`, `examples.md`, `scripts/`) loaded on-demand:
+    └── helper.py      # Executed, not loaded into context

+**Cohezion Implication**: PRIME skills can be restructured for progressive disclosure — keep the skill description tight for auto-discovery, move detailed operational instructions to supporting files. This could reduce Cohezion's baseline context footprint by 80%+.
+The frontmatter fields create a 2x2 control matrix for skill activation:
+| | User Can Invoke | User Cannot Invoke |
+| **Model Can Invoke** | Default (most skills) | `user-invocable: false` — background knowledge |
+| **Model Cannot Invoke** | `disable-model-invocation: true` — explicit workflows | Invisible (not useful) |
+- `allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob` — tool whitelist when skill is active
+- `model: haiku` — model override for cost optimization
+- `context: fork` — run in isolated subagent context
+- `agent: Explore` — specify subagent type for forked execution
+- `hooks:` — lifecycle hooks scoped to skill activation
+**Cohezion Compound Engineering Pattern**: Combine these controls:
+- **PRIME research skills** → `context: fork`, `agent: Explore`, `model: haiku` → cheap, isolated research
+- **Domain knowledge** → `user-invocable: false` → background context Claude applies automatically
+- **Sovereignty checks** → `hooks: PreToolUse` in frontmatter → Constitution enforcement scoped to skill lifecycle
+The plugin architecture enables a three-tier agent hierarchy:
+Plugin settings.json agent → Main Thread Agent (sovereign system prompt)
+    ├── Skill with context: fork → Forked Subagent (isolated task)
+    ├── Agent tool → Custom Subagent (specialist with tool whitelist)
+**Official Pattern (code-review plugin)**: 5 parallel Sonnet agents with distinct specializations:
+4. Validation agents for each finding (parallel, model-appropriate)
+**Key Design Constraint**: "3-4 subagents maximum" — beyond this, coordination overhead exceeds parallelism benefit. Each task should target 5-15 minutes of work.
+| `CompoundExecutor` | Main thread agent with sovereign system prompt |
+| Expert Domain Lattice | Agents with specialized tool whitelists + model overrides |
+Hooks create a **deterministic feedback loop** that maps directly to the compound engineering cycle:
+SessionStart hook → Initialize journey, load vault context
+PreCompact hook → State preservation before context loss
+SessionEnd hook → Journey completion, metrics flush, skill refinement trigger

+**Key Architectural Insight**: The `Stop` hook enables autonomous agent loops. The `ralph-wiggum` official plugin demonstrates this — it creates a `/ralph-loop` command and a `Stop` hook that prevents termination until completion criteria are met. Combined with `TeammateIdle` for work distribution, this enables fully autonomous compound engineering cycles.

+**PreCompact as State Bridge**: The `PreCompact` hook fires before context compression — the exact point where Cohezion's context continuation protocol needs to save state. A hook here could automatically write continuation files before any context is lost.
+Skills support shell command preprocessing via `` !`command` `` syntax — commands execute before the skill content is sent to Claude:
+This enables **live system state injection** — every time the skill activates, it fetches fresh data from Cohezion's compound systems. No stale context, no manual updates.

+A critical insight from the Trail of Bits analysis: **"Hooks are structured prompt injection at opportune times — guardrails, not walls."** They intercept tool calls, inject context, block known-bad patterns, and steer agent behavior, but they are not a security boundary against determined adversaries.
+| **Constitution** | `PreToolUse` hook → deny actions violating Charter | Deterministic, guaranteed |
+| **Alignment** | `UserPromptSubmit` agent hook → semantic analysis | Probabilistic, model-dependent |
+| **Observability** | `PostToolUse` async hook → metrics/audit trail | Non-blocking, comprehensive |

+**Hook Snapshotting**: Hooks are captured at session start and frozen. Mid-session modifications trigger review warnings. This prevents runtime hook tampering — a Cohezion plugin's Constitutional hooks cannot be altered once a session begins.

Here are the search results on migrating an existing `.claude/` directory (skills, commands, hooks) to the Claude Code plugin system:

## Migration from `.claude/` to Plugin

If you already have skills or hooks in your `.claude/` directory, you can convert them into a plugin for easier sharing and distribution.

### Why Migrate?

You've built your skills, wired up your hooks, and assembled your subagents. Now your `.claude/` directory is a sprawling mess of Markdown files that only you understand, and sharing it with a teammate means committing your deeply personal CLAUDE.md or handing them a zip file. There's a better way — plugins are how Claude Code goes from solo power tool to a shareable, versioned, installable ecosystem.

### Two Approaches

Claude Code supports two ways to add custom skills, agents, and hooks: standalone configuration in `.claude/` for quick iteration, or plugins with namespaced skills like `/my-plugin:hello` (namespacing prevents conflicts between plugins).

### Migration Steps

1. **Create the plugin manifest**: You can convert existing `.claude/` skills and hooks into a plugin. Create a `plugin.json` with metadata, then copy your directories — e.g., `cp -r .claude/commands my-plugin/`, `cp -r .claude/agents my-plugin/`, `cp -r .claude/skills my-plugin/`.

2. **Migrate hooks**: Create `my-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` with your hooks configuration. Copy the hooks object from your `.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json`, since the format is the same.

3. **Test**: For local development, start Claude Code with `claude --plugin-dir ./your-plugin` to test without installation.

### Plugin Directory Structure

Each plugin follows the standard Claude Code plugin structure:
```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json        # Plugin metadata
├── commands/              # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/                # Specialized agents (optional)
├── skills/                # Agent Skills (optional)
├── hooks/                 # Event handlers (optional)
├── .mcp.json              # External tool configuration (optional)
└── README.md              # Plugin documentation
```

### Common Mistake

Don't put `commands/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, or `hooks/` inside the `.claude-plugin/` directory. Only `plugin.json` goes inside `.claude-plugin/`. All other directories must be at the plugin root level.

Here are the search results on migrating an existing `.claude/` directory (skills, commands, hooks) to the Claude Code plugin system:

## Migration from `.claude/` to Plugin

If you already have skills or hooks in your `.claude/` directory, you can convert them into a plugin for easier sharing and distribution.

### Why Migrate?

You've built your skills, wired up your hooks, and assembled your subagents. Now your `.claude/` directory is a sprawling mess of Markdown files that only you understand, and sharing it with a teammate means committing your deeply personal CLAUDE.md or handing them a zip file. There's a better way — plugins are how Claude Code goes from solo power tool to a shareable, versioned, installable ecosystem.

### Two Approaches

Claude Code supports two ways to add custom skills, agents, and hooks: standalone configuration in `.claude/` for quick iteration, or plugins with namespaced skills like `/my-plugin:hello` (namespacing prevents conflicts between plugins).

### Migration Steps

1. **Create the plugin manifest**: You can convert existing `.claude/` skills and hooks into a plugin. Create a `plugin.json` with metadata, then copy your directories — e.g., `cp -r .claude/commands my-plugin/`, `cp -r .claude/agents my-plugin/`, `cp -r .claude/skills my-plugin/`.

2. **Migrate hooks**: Create `my-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` with your hooks configuration. Copy the hooks object from your `.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json`, since the format is the same.

3. **Test**: For local development, start Claude Code with `claude --plugin-dir ./your-plugin` to test without installation.

### Plugin Directory Structure

Each plugin follows the standard Claude Code plugin structure:
```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json        # Plugin metadata
├── commands/              # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/                # Specialized agents (optional)
├── skills/                # Agent Skills (optional)
├── hooks/                 # Event handlers (optional)
├── .mcp.json              # External tool configuration (optional)
└── README.md              # Plugin documentation
```

### Common Mistake

Don't put `commands/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, or `hooks/` inside the `.claude-plugin/` directory. Only `plugin.json` goes inside `.claude-plugin/`. All other directories must be at the plugin root level.

Here's a comprehensive overview of creating and distributing a private Claude Code plugin marketplace for your team in 2026:

## What Is a Plugin Marketplace?

A plugin marketplace is a catalog that lets you distribute plugins to others. Marketplaces provide centralized discovery, version tracking, automatic updates, and support for multiple source types (git repositories, local paths, and more).

A plugin marketplace is a centralized catalog that distributes Claude Code extensions across teams and communities. Think of it as an app store for Claude Code.

## Creating a Marketplace

The process involves two main steps:

1. Creating plugins: build one or more plugins with commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or LSP servers. This guide assumes you already have plugins to distribute.
2. Creating a marketplace file: define a `marketplace.json` that lists your plugins and where to find them.

Plugins are just directories with Markdown and JSON files. No build step, no compilation, no registry approval required. Test locally with `--plugin-dir` and share via GitHub.

## Distribution Methods

### Git Repository (GitHub, GitLab, etc.)
Users add your marketplace with `/plugin marketplace add owner/repo`, providing built-in version control, issue tracking, and team collaboration features. Any git hosting service works, such as GitLab, Bitbucket, and self-hosted servers.

### For Enterprise/Team Plans (Cowork)
Plugin marketplaces allow Team and Enterprise plan owners to distribute curated plugins to everyone in their organization through Cowork. You create a marketplace, add plugins to it, and control exactly which plugins your team members can see.

There are two ways to add plugins:
- **Manual upload** — Upload individual plugin ZIP files through the admin UI. Best for quick iteration, one-off tools, or teams that don't use GitHub for plugin development.
- **GitHub syncing** — Connect a private GitHub repository and Cowork automatically syncs plugins from it. Best when multiple developers collaborate on plugins or you want version-controlled updates.

**Important:** Your repository must be private or internal — public repos aren't allowed for organization marketplaces. Repos hosted on custom GitHub Enterprise Server instances aren't supported. Your repo must be hosted on github.com.

## Private Repository Support

Claude Code supports installing plugins from private repositories. For manual installation and updates, Claude Code uses your existing git credential helpers. If `git clone` works for a private repository in your terminal, it works in Claude Code too.

Common credential helpers include `gh auth login` for GitHub, macOS Keychain, and `git-credential-store`.

### Auto-Updates for Private Repos
Background auto-updates run at startup without credential helpers, since interactive prompts would block Claude Code from starting. To enable auto-updates for private marketplaces, set the appropriate authentication token in your environment.

### Local Clone Approach
The most reliable approach for private marketplaces is to clone the repository locally and register the local path. This avoids authentication issues and gives you instant updates during development.

## Enterprise Features (February 2026 Updates)

Enterprises can now build private marketplaces to distribute custom plugins across their organizations. Admins control which plugins teams can access, including organization-specific marketplaces and private GitHub repositories as plugin sources (currently in private beta).

Admins can also source plugins from private GitHub repositories — a feature currently in private beta. This means a company's internal development team can write and version plugins in a private repo and publish them to the internal marketplace without routing code through Anthropic's infrastructure. That distinction matters significantly for IP-sensitive organizations.

Admins can now set up plugins from starter templates or build them from scratch, with Claude guiding you through setup by asking questions to tailor skills, commands, and connectors (MCPs) to your company.

## Team Configuration

To auto-configure the marketplace for your team, you can add it to your project's settings. Configure automatic marketplace installation for your team by adding `.claude/settings.json` to your projects with the `extraKnownMarketplaces` field. When team members trust the repository folder, Claude Code automatically installs the marketplace.

## Useful Resources

- A GitHub template (`ivan-magda/claude-code-plugin-template`) lets you create and distribute Claude Code plugins for your team or community, providing everything you need to build a plugin marketplace — from scaffolding and validation to CI/CD automation.
- Anthropic also provides a Plugin Dev Toolkit (an official plugin itself) with an 8-phase guided workflow for building plugins. Run `/plugin-dev:create-plugin` and it walks you through the entire process.

## Technology Stack Analysis

### Plugin System Architecture

Claude Code plugins are **self-contained directory bundles** that extend the Claude Code CLI through six orthogonal extension points. The architecture follows a composition-over-inheritance model where each plugin is a directory containing a manifest (`plugin.json`) plus optional component directories. Plugins are loaded at startup, cached at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`, and namespaced to prevent conflicts.

**Core Architectural Insight**: The plugin system is *not* a traditional code-level plugin API with interfaces to implement. It's a **declarative configuration system** — markdown files, JSON manifests, and shell scripts. No TypeScript compilation. No build step. Just files in the right directory structure.

_Confidence: HIGH — verified against official docs and 13 official plugins in the repository_
_Source: [Claude Code Plugin Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Six Extension Points (The Plugin Primitives)

| Extension | Weight | Loading | Format | Cohezion Analog |
|-----------|--------|---------|--------|-----------------|
| **Skills** | Lightest | Model-invoked (automatic) | `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | PRIME skills |
| **Commands** | Light | User-invoked (`/name`) | `commands/<name>.md` | `/spec`, `/commit` |
| **Agents** | Medium | Model/user-invoked | `agents/<name>.md` with frontmatter | Subagent types |
| **Hooks** | Medium | Event-driven (automatic) | `hooks/hooks.json` → shell/python | `.claude/hooks/` |
| **MCP Servers** | Heavy | Auto-started on plugin enable | `.mcp.json` | `.mcp.json` |
| **LSP Servers** | Heavy | Auto-started on plugin enable | `.lsp.json` | N/A (new) |

**Key Design Properties:**
- **Skills** are the token-cheapest extension — they only load into context when Claude determines relevance. Frontmatter controls: `disable-model-invocation: true` makes them user-only.
- **Agents** have full subagent semantics: their own system prompt, model selection (`model: sonnet|opus|haiku`), tool restrictions (`tools: Glob, Grep, Read`), and color identifiers.
- **Hooks** support 13 event types including `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `Stop`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `TaskCompleted`, and `TeammateIdle`.
- **Hook types**: `command` (shell), `prompt` (LLM evaluation), and `agent` (agentic verifier with tool access).

_Source: [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference), [Official GitHub](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins)_

### Plugin Manifest Schema (`plugin.json`)

```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name",           // REQUIRED: kebab-case identifier + namespace
  "version": "1.0.0",              // semver
  "description": "Brief purpose",
  "author": { "name": "...", "email": "...", "url": "..." },
  "homepage": "...",
  "repository": "...",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["tag1", "tag2"],
  "commands": ["./custom/cmd.md"],  // Additional paths (supplement defaults)
  "agents": "./custom/agents/",
  "skills": "./custom/skills/",
  "hooks": "./config/hooks.json",   // Or inline object
  "mcpServers": "./mcp-config.json", // Or inline object
  "lspServers": "./.lsp.json",
  "outputStyles": "./styles/"
}
```

**Critical detail**: Custom paths *supplement* default directories, they don't replace them. If `commands/` exists at root AND `"commands": ["./extra/"]` is specified, both are loaded.

**Environment variable**: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolves to the plugin's absolute installation path. Essential for hook scripts and MCP server configs.

_Source: [Plugins Reference — Manifest Schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Agent Definition Format

Agent markdown files use YAML frontmatter for configuration:

```yaml
---
name: code-architect
description: Designs feature architectures by analyzing codebase patterns
tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, WebSearch
model: sonnet
color: green
---

System prompt content follows...
```

**Key fields**: `name`, `description`, `tools` (whitelist), `model` (override), `color` (UI identifier).

**Pattern from official `feature-dev` plugin**: 3 specialized agents (`code-explorer`, `code-architect`, `code-reviewer`) with distinct tool restrictions and model assignments. The architect agent uses Sonnet with read-only tools, demonstrating least-privilege design.

_Source: [feature-dev agents](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/feature-dev/agents)_

### Hook System Architecture

Hooks are the most powerful extension point for autonomous behavior. The `hooks.json` format:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/script.py"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Exit code semantics for `PreToolUse`**: Exit 0 = allow tool, Exit 2 = block tool and show stderr as message. This enables **guardrail plugins** that can prevent operations.

**13 Available Events:**

| Event | Trigger | Cohezion Relevance |
|-------|---------|-------------------|
| `SessionStart` | Session begins | Context injection, sovereignty checks |
| `PreToolUse` | Before any tool | Security guardrails, alignment checks |
| `PostToolUse` | After successful tool | Auto-formatting, metrics recording |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | After tool failure | Error tracking, circuit breakers |
| `Stop` | Agent attempts to stop | Autonomous loop control |
| `SubagentStart` | Subagent spawns | Journey tracking, resource governance |
| `SubagentStop` | Subagent completion | Metrics collection |
| `PreCompact` | Before context compression | State preservation |
| `TaskCompleted` | Task marked complete | Verification triggers |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User sends prompt | Input validation |
| `TeammateIdle` | Team agent goes idle | Load balancing |
| `Notification` | System notification | Alert routing |
| `PermissionRequest` | Permission dialog shown | Auto-approval policies |

_Source: [security-guidance plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/security-guidance), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Settings System (`settings.json`)

Plugins can ship default settings that activate when the plugin is enabled:

```json
{ "agent": "security-reviewer" }
```

This **overrides the main thread agent** — the plugin's agent becomes the primary conversational interface with its own system prompt, tools, and model. Settings from `settings.json` take priority over those in `plugin.json`.

**Implication for Cohezion**: A plugin could activate a "Cohezion Sovereign Agent" as the default, embedding the Charter and Constitution into every session automatically.

_Confidence: HIGH — verified in official docs_
_Source: [Plugins Docs — Settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins)_

### Distribution and Marketplace Architecture

Plugins distribute through **marketplaces** — Git repositories containing a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` that indexes available plugins:

**Installation scopes:**

| Scope | Location | Sharing |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `user` | `~/.claude/settings.json` | Personal, all projects |
| `project` | `.claude/settings.json` | Team-shared via VCS |
| `local` | `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project-only, gitignored |
| `managed` | Managed settings | Read-only |

**CLI commands**: `claude plugin install`, `uninstall`, `enable`, `disable`, `update` — all supporting `--scope` flag.

**Caching**: Marketplace plugins are copied to `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`. Path traversal outside plugin root is blocked. Symlinks are honored during copy (enables shared dependencies).

_Source: [Plugin Marketplaces](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces), [Plugins Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)_

### Agent SDK Integration

The Claude Agent SDK (Python + TypeScript) can **programmatically load plugins** into agent sessions:

- Plugins loaded via `--plugin-dir` or marketplace
- Commands auto-namespaced: `plugin-name:command-name`
- MCP servers auto-started
- Skills auto-discovered by model
- Custom tools via in-process MCP servers (Python functions or TypeScript `tool()` helpers)

**Implication**: Cohezion's `CompoundExecutor` could leverage the Agent SDK to load plugins programmatically, adding compound engineering capabilities to any Claude agent session.

_Source: [Agent SDK Plugins Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/plugins), [Agent SDK Overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview)_

### Technology Adoption and Ecosystem Scale

- **9,000+ plugins** across official marketplace, community sites, and GitHub (as of Feb 2026)
- **13 official Anthropic plugins** in the `anthropics/claude-code` repository
- **400+ curated extensions** on buildwithclaude.com

_Source: [Composio](https://composio.dev/blog/top-claude-code-plugins), [AI Tool Analysis](https://aitoolanalysis.com/claude-code-plugins/), [Build with Claude](https://www.buildwithclaude.com/plugins)_

### Cohezion Alignment Assessment (Technology Stack)
